acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). The joint protocol's sub-condition (c) - candidate successes strictly exceeding cumulative - remains NOT carried over as a graded sub-condition, for the reason recorded in the bounded-authority protocol: it was that cycle's headline test of a different selected limitation (engagement sparsity) and grading it again here would conflate distinct limitations in one experiment. Cumulative's, the joint candidate's, and the bounded candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside this criterion in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. This cycle's headline test is criterion 2.

acceptance_criteria.name: recovery_engagement_restored_and_selective_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded bounded candidate FAILed engagement on its additional cohort (2 of 6 return-A onset states taken, 3 of 6 would-fire-but-disarmed at corroboration count exactly 1), and this cycle exists to answer that failure. Graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY (no TEST outcomes), per cohort: (a) the recovery branch is TAKEN (joint_count >= 1, recovery armed, acting source retained_archive) in at least 4 of the 6 return-A onset seed-checkpoint states (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds) - the low edge of this protocol's design interval of approx 4-5 of 6 under the long-disagreement leg, one below the unexpired joint candidate's graded 5 of 6 and materially above the bounded candidate's additional-cohort 2 of 6, as derived in threshold_justification; AND (b) the recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 B1 onset seed-checkpoint states. B2 and control engagement counts are reported, not graded under this criterion (B2 non-recovery is a pre-registered expectation, and control engagement is graded downstream under criterion 6). Would-fire-but-disarmed counts at onset are reported alongside, split by which authority leg armed each taken state (no-disagreement / corroboration / long), so the records distinguish long-leg restoration from corroboration-leg luck.

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint protocol. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. Carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded release guard for this experiment - the graded joint candidate FAILed its checkpoint-32 criterion on both cohorts and the graded bounded candidate restored it (additional fully, development to one residual late state); this cycle's fix must not give that release back. Per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (the bounded protocol's measurable form, carried over unchanged; the bounded candidate's gaps were -13 development and 0 additional, the joint candidate's -19 and -9), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive or abstained) in at most 1 state - the direct records-level measure that the gate's authority has actually expired late, counting both late routes (the carried-over corroboration leg and the new long leg), as distinct from its downstream totals happening to pass. Sub-condition (c)'s design expectation is approx 0-1 states per cohort (see threshold_justification).

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_downstream_selectivity
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. Identical in form to the graded guard's criterion 5, the retained-recovery protocol's criterion 6, and the joint protocol's criterion 6. Expiry-flag values on the control arm are recorded and reported; the flag itself is not graded here, the downstream totals are.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, joint_count, opposed_count, matched_count, concordant_count, archive_matched_count, the full authority record incl. per-span local/archive majorities, comparable/disagreeing counts, stable_disagreement flag, per-span preceding-window records, preceding comparable/disagreeing counts, preceding stable-disagreement flag, long-disagreement flag, per-event last-8 archive-concordance flags, recent_concordant_count, per-branch armed and would-fire flags, branch taken, recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

baselines.in: all criteria comparisons as named; every candidate-vs-recent8 difference is attributable to the decision rule (now including its expiry condition) alone
baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and the candidate's own acting model: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; engagement, onset, and checkpoint-32 comparisons in the report (its totals are reference points, not PASS/FAIL comparators in the criteria, whose bounds are absolute or against recent8/guard/cumulative/frozen_A as named)
baselines.name: joint_concordance_recovery
baselines.role: JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): identical acting model, identical immediate signal, identical archive, identical joint recovery test, identical abstention branch, differing ONLY in that its branches have NO expiry condition at all. Its realized return-A engagement (5 of 6 onset states on both of its cohorts) is the level criterion 2 must restore, and its checkpoint-32 totals are the unexpired reference for criterion 5.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1-5 comparisons in the report (its totals are the decisive authority comparison, not PASS/FAIL comparators beyond the criteria as named)
baselines.name: bounded_authority_joint_recovery
baselines.role: BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory, the preceding experiment's candidate (graded Failed): identical acting model, identical immediate signal, identical archive, identical joint recovery test, identical abstention authority, and identical local-disagreement and corroboration recovery legs, differing ONLY in that its recovery authority has NO long-disagreement leg. This is the decisive comparison for this experiment: candidate-vs-bounded-candidate differences isolate the long leg alone, at onset (criteria 1-4, above all criterion 2) and at checkpoint 32 (criterion 5).

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; return-A and checkpoint-32 reference comparisons in the report (not a PASS/FAIL comparator in this protocol's criteria - see the grading note on criterion 1)
baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events. Plain cumulative retention dominated the pooled retained-recovery candidate and trailed the joint candidate's firing states not at all (identical per firing state); it remains the strongest simple retained comparator and is reported at every checkpoint, including at return-A and checkpoint 32.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1, 3, and 4 comparisons
baselines.name: evidence_opposition_guard
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory (graded Demonstrated): the candidate's own immediate signal and acting model, with abstention as its only protective response, released by checkpoint 32 on both of its cohorts by window-sliding. Criteria 1, 3, and 4 hold the candidate to the guard's harm levels on the same cohort.

baselines.name: evidence_opposition_retained_recovery
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, the pooled both-events candidate (graded Failed): the engagement-sparsity reference point.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criterion 1 comparison
baselines.name: frozen_A
baselines.role: Relation model fitted on the first 192 events, never updated. The recovery target reference at return_A: what pure retained pre-switch knowledge scores there.

baselines.name: recent32
baselines.role: Relation model on the last 32 observed events.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; preceding-learner comparison
baselines.name: gated_archive_prequential
baselines.role: GatedArchivePrequentialMemory (graded Failed / regression): the earlier archive-routing candidate.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; productivity floor reference
baselines.name: always_abstain
baselines.role: Abstains on every TEST task: 0 successes, 0 harmful actions, all tasks failed-by-abstention. The trivially safe control.

baselines.name: untrained_random
baselines.role: Independent seeded random TEST action policy; gathers no training outcomes.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint, labeled privileged
baselines.name: privileged_expected_oracle
baselines.role: PRIVILEGED reference only: knows the expected hidden rule (not the realized stochastic flip). Never a realizable baseline and never counted in any PASS/FAIL comparison.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled return-A onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 6 per stage per cohort at checkpoints 2 and 4, and 9 switch-stage states per cohort at checkpoint 32.

budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, joint, and bounded-authority protocols. Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the bounded candidate's release mechanism, carried over unchanged, not a budget violation.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The disarmed-abstention tradeoff at return onset (expected failure mode 4) is charged against these criteria, not excused from them.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Long leg fails to register at return onset: preceding-window span majorities are computed from ~26 events (~2-4 per span), so on some return states the preceding window's disagreement may fall to or below half of comparable spans by sampling noise, leaving recovery armed only through the bounded candidate's legs - engagement falls back toward the bounded candidate's starved level (2-3 of 6 on an unlucky cohort) and criterion 2 (floor 4 of 6) FAILs even though the mechanism works as designed on average. That outcome would show the disagreement-age signal is too noisy at this window scale - an informative, pre-registered result, not a protocol defect.

Preceding-window self-inclusion bias: the preceding window (events[N-52:N-26]) is a subset of the archive (events[:N-26]) it is compared against (26 of ~266+ archive events at return onset), biasing preceding span majorities toward the archive's and therefore against the long flag. If this bias binds, return engagement again falls toward the corroboration leg's level and criterion 2 FAILs; the bias direction is conservative (against arming) and is recorded in the protocol rather than corrected by a fitted adjustment.

Residual late false recovery, two routes: (a) the corroboration leg is carried over unchanged, so a late window with recent_concordant_count >= 2 and a joint event re-arms exactly as in the graded bounded candidate (its development B2-32 state at count exactly 2 scored 0/16 vs recent8 13/3 - the entire remaining development checkpoint-32 deficit there); (b) the new long leg can misfire late if the preceding window at a B1/B2 checkpoint-32 state registers stable disagreement by majority noise (design approx 0.10-0.20 per state before the joint test is applied). Either route is graded by criterion 5's records sub-condition (at most 1 non-recent8 branch state in 9) and its productivity sub-condition.

Abstention disarmed at return onset (carried over unchanged from the bounded candidate, BY DESIGN): because the local segment at a return is the reversed segment, the stable-disagreement flag is set there and the abstention fallback cannot fire at return-A onset states. Non-engaging return states therefore act through stale recent8 instead of abstaining, raising return-A and pooled onset harm; criteria 3 and 4 may FAIL on this tradeoff even if engagement is restored. It is charged against those criteria, not excused, exactly as in the preceding protocol.

opposed_count == 0 return-A blind spot (recorded, NOT this cycle's selected limitation): a return state whose newest events agree with the already-partly-slid reference window cannot engage recovery under the joint test, under any authority condition. It accounted for the entire exceed-cumulative deficit in the joint experiment (-4 / -12) and for 1 of 6 additional return-A states in the bounded experiment (joint-silent, seed 343017 at checkpoint 2). It is reported from the records in this experiment and is deliberately not graded away and not repaired here; repairing it is a separate hypothesis requiring its own protocol.

Short-intervening-segment scope limit (stated, not hidden): the long leg requires the archive-disagreeing segment to fill a full 52-event lookback. A return after an intervening segment shorter than 52 events cannot arm through this leg and falls back to the corroboration leg, with its known checkpoint-2 starvation. This simulator's return geometry (64-event B1 segment before return_A) is inside the leg's scope; the limit bounds the claim, and no part of the grading credits the leg outside it.

Return-A archive harm at scale: as in the preceding experiments, archive play in firing states carries nonzero harm (design approx 4-8 per firing state); with engagement restored to 5-6 firing states, pooled return-A harm can land above the 60-percent-of-recent8 ceiling (the joint candidate: 40 vs ceiling 37.8 on its development cohort) and fail criterion 4 even when engagement succeeds.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, the graded retained-recovery candidate, and the graded joint candidate.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded retained-recovery and joint candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, expiry records - local comparable/disagreeing span counts, stable-disagreement flag, preceding-window span records, preceding comparable/disagreeing counts, preceding stable-disagreement flag, long-disagreement flag, per-event last-8 archive-concordance flags, recent_concordant_count, per-branch armed and would-fire flags - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive). (2) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2 AND the abstention branch is armed, abstain (choose returns None), exactly the graded guard's protective response. (3) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Onset protection, return engagement, and late release are separated by how LONG the archive has been wrong, not by how strongly the newest window matches it. While no stable archive-disagreeing local segment exists, the stream has not yet established a current rule the archive lacks, so both protective branches keep the authority the graded joint candidate gave them - this covers B1 onset (local window still the original rule, agreeing with the archive), B2 onset (local window still the return-A segment, agreeing with the archive), and stationary evidence (local and archive agree throughout), exactly as in the bounded candidate. Under stable disagreement the bounded candidate armed recovery only through last-8 corroboration, which starves at checkpoint 2 because only 2 of the 8 acting-window events follow the returned rule. The long-disagreement leg reads the one quantity that separates a genuine return from a late flip-back in the graded records: at a return, the disagreeing segment is the full intervening segment, stable across BOTH the local and the preceding window - the archive rule has been absent for at least 52 events and the newest archive-concordant, reference-opposed event is a segment-scale event. Late in B1/B2 the archive rule was current within the preceding window (the original segment's tail at B1, the return-A segment's tail at B2), so preceding disagreement is not stable and authority there still rests on the corroboration leg alone, whose late firing rate the bounded experiment measured. Abstention is deliberately NOT re-armed by the long leg: recovery, not abstention, is the return response, and a non-engaging return state acts through recent8 rather than abstaining - the bounded candidate's pre-registered tradeoff, kept and graded under criteria 3 and 4.
fixed_parameters.expiry_condition: The bounded candidate's authority condition, EXTENDED by one new leg (C); legs (A) and (B) are IDENTICAL to the graded bounded-authority candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned. All quantities are computed from the observed reported stream only, at every decision, using the SAME span-majority machinery (strictly-highest reported class among events of equal span; tie or empty gives null; only progress/damage majorities are comparable): (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT. The local window is the last 26 observed events (the reference window plus the newest window, indices N-26 .. N-1). For each distinct span value s present in the local window, let local_majority(s) be the strictly-highest reported class among local-window events of span s and archive_majority(s) the strictly-highest reported class among archive events (events[:N-26]) of span s. Span s is COMPARABLE if both majorities are progress or damage, and DISAGREEING if comparable and the two majorities differ. Let comparable_span_count = C and disagreeing_span_count = D. The stable-disagreement flag is set iff C >= 1 AND D * 2 > C (a strict majority of comparable spans disagree). (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE. For each of the last 8 observed events, the event is counted archive-concordant iff it is archive-matched and its reported class equals archive_majority(span(event)), using the SAME current archive as above (not a per-position archive). recent_concordant_count is in 0..8. (C) PRECEDING-WINDOW ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT - NEW, the single changed element of this experiment. The preceding window is the 26 observed events immediately before the local window, indices max(0, N-52) .. N-27 (events[max(0,N-52):N-26]). For each distinct span value s present in the preceding window, let preceding_majority(s) be the strictly-highest reported class among preceding-window events of span s and archive_majority(s) as in (A). Span s is PRECEDING-COMPARABLE if both majorities are progress or damage, and PRECEDING-DISAGREEING if preceding-comparable and the two majorities differ. Let preceding_comparable_span_count = C2 and preceding_disagreeing_span_count = D2. The preceding stable-disagreement flag is set iff C2 >= 1 AND D2 * 2 > C2, the SAME strict-majority rule as (A), carried over unchanged. The LONG-DISAGREEMENT flag is set iff the stable-disagreement flag (A) AND the preceding stable-disagreement flag (C) are both set. BRANCH AUTHORITY: the ABSTENTION branch is ARMED iff the stable-disagreement flag is NOT set - IDENTICAL to the graded bounded candidate; the long leg does not touch abstention. The RECOVERY branch is ARMED iff the stable-disagreement flag is NOT set OR recent_concordant_count >= 2 OR the long-disagreement flag is set - the first two legs IDENTICAL to the graded bounded candidate, the third is this experiment's single new element. When a branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever its trigger count says; a decision that would have taken a disarmed branch falls through to the next branch in the decision order, exactly as if its trigger had not fired, and the record carries both the would-have-fired flag and the armed flag so the authority's effect is graded from the records alone. No other input enters the condition: no fitted probability, no phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded evidence-opposition guard, the graded retained-recovery candidate, and the graded joint candidate, reused unchanged and not re-tuned: newest window = last 2 observed events; reference window = the 24 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-26 .. N-3). For each newest event, the reference expectation is the strictly-highest reported outcome class among reference events of equal span (tie or empty gives null); an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different. opposed_count in 0..2. No fitted probabilities anywhere in any signal.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded joint candidate, unchanged: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT (per the unchanged archive test) AND reference-OPPOSED (per the unchanged immediate signal) - both flags on the SAME event. joint_count is the number of joint newest events (0..2).
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: Both signals together require a 2-event newest window, a full 24-event reference window, and at least 1 archive event: at least 27 observed events. Below 27 events neither signal is evaluable and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable). The preceding window of leg (C) is events[max(0,N-52):N-26]: below 52 events it is a partial window (below 27 events it is empty and the preceding flag is unset, as no span is comparable). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so both windows are full and the fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery and joint candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose). The recovery model never includes the reference window or the newest window.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery and joint candidates: every observed event BEFORE the reference window, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. It is not a snapshot, not phase-segmented, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates and the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). Span-majority reliability (carried over from the bounded-authority protocol): the archive holds ~214+ events at every graded checkpoint (~20+ per span value across the engineered span bands), so its per-span majorities are the majority rule's class with probability near 1. A 26-event window holds ~2-4 events per span, so a window per-span majority follows its segment's rule with design probability approx 0.75-0.90 per span (majority of 2-4 samples each agreeing with the segment rule at the composed agreement rate approx 0.84 after the 0.1625 disagreement rate from 1/8 stochastic + 1/20 report flips). Where a window's segment rule is the REVERSE of the archive's, per-span disagreement is approx 0.75-0.90 and a strict-majority flag over the comparable spans (typically 5-8) fires with design probability approx 0.90; where the segment rule EQUALS the archive's, per-span disagreement is approx 0.10-0.25 and the same flag fires with design probability well under 0.05. Long-leg arithmetic at return onset: the preceding window lies entirely inside the 64-event intervening reversed segment, so its flag fires at the reverse-segment rate approx 0.90, and the local flag is already set there by construction of the return geometry (graded records: set in 6 of 6 return-A onset states on both bounded cohorts); the long leg therefore arms recovery at approx 0.85-0.90 of return-A onset states, and combined with the joint test's per-state engagement (graded 5 of 6 for the unexpired gate, per-state design approx 0.70-0.80) gives recovery TAKEN at approx 4-5 of 6 return-A onset states - hence criterion 2's engagement floor is set at 4 of 6, the low edge of that design interval and one below the unexpired gate's realized 5 of 6, so a criterion-2 FAIL means the long leg did not restore engagement even to the floor, an informative pre-registered outcome, not a protocol defect to be repaired after seeing scores. Late arithmetic: at B1/B2 checkpoint 32 the preceding window is dominated by an archive-rule segment (approx 20 of 26 events: the original segment's tail at B1, the return-A segment's tail at B2), so its per-span majorities follow the archive rule on most spans and the preceding flag's design firing probability is approx 0.10-0.20 (it requires a strict majority of comparable spans to err in the same direction); recovery late additionally requires a joint event in the newest window (graded late rate approx 0.10-0.25 per state), so a late false recovery through the long leg has design probability approx 0.01-0.05 per late state - hence criterion 5's records sub-condition still allows at most 1 non-recent8 branch state among the 9 checkpoint-32 switch-stage states per cohort, counting BOTH late routes (the carried-over corroboration leg realized 1 such state on the bounded development cohort). Self-inclusion note: the preceding window contributes 26 of ~266+ archive events at return onset, shifting archive span majorities toward the preceding segment's rule by at most a few counts per span against ~20+ archive events per span; the bias is against the long flag (conservative) and is accepted uncorrected rather than fitted away. The abstention threshold (opposed_count == 2), the recovery threshold (joint_count >= 1), the strict-majority disagreement rule (D * 2 > C), and the corroboration count >= 2 are carried over UNCHANGED from the graded bounded candidate; the only new threshold is the SAME strict-majority rule applied to the preceding window - no new fitted constant is introduced.

candidate.name: LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, the graded EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, the graded JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory, and the graded BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

capability_under_test: Return-onset authority starvation: whether a recovery-authority condition that does not starve at the earliest onset checkpoint - arming recovery under stable local-archive disagreement when that disagreement is LONG (stable in both the local 26-event window and the preceding 26-event window, i.e. the archive has been wrong for the entire 52-event lookback), while still expiring late (checkpoint-32 productivity within 8 successes of recent8 and at most 1 non-recent8 branch state in 9, from records) - can restore return-A engagement to at least the graded joint candidate's level (5 of 6 return-A onset states) and keep return-A harm at or below 60 percent of recent8, against recent8, cumulative, frozen_A, the evidence-opposition guard, the graded joint-concordance candidate, and the graded bounded-authority candidate as baselines. Priority 1 items 2 + 3 + 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge and first-contact overconfidence.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 are the graded onset window; 8 and 16 report persistence costs; 32 grades release. In this experiment criterion 2 at checkpoints 2 and 4 is the PRIMARY criterion - the graded bounded candidate starved exactly there on its additional cohort - and criterion 5 at checkpoint 32 is the co-graded release guard. Checkpoint values are benchmark bookkeeping only: the learner never receives k, a stage name, or any elapsed-since-switch count (see permitted_observations); the long-disagreement leg is a span-majority comparison over two observed windows, not a count of post-switch events. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world.

grading.failed: Criterion 2 FAILs on the additional cohort, or any of criteria 1, 3, 4, or 5 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary. Criterion 2 is reported first among the criteria in the grading report, as this experiment's primary criterion; criterion 5 (release) is reported second, as its co-graded guard.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, routing, expiry, and now disagreement-age rules). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, joint test, disagreement, corroboration, and long-disagreement conditions, and decision rule are all designer-supplied. A PASS would demonstrate disagreement-age-bounded gate authority - onset recovery that stays armed across a long intervening segment and expires after a short one - in this simulator only, not general regime identification (the archive is global and unsegmented; B2 recovery is pre-registered as not expected; returns after intervening segments shorter than 52 events are outside the long leg's scope), not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criterion 2 and criterion 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 1, 3, 4, 5, or 6 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the candidate's checkpoint-32 successes fall below the graded bounded candidate's checkpoint-32 deficit pattern (i.e. below recent8 - 13 on either cohort, the bounded candidate's worse cohort gap), or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.

hypothesis: The bounded candidate's corroboration leg counts archive-concordant events among the last 8, but at checkpoint 2 of a return only 2 of those 8 events follow the returned rule, so the count leans on flip-back concordance among the 6 preceding reversed events and lands at exactly 1 in the states that most need recovery. The graded decision records show this is not fixable by re-thresholding the existing counts: the profile (joint_count 1, opposed_count 1, concordant_count 1, recent_concordant_count 1, stable disagreement set) occurs BOTH at additional-cohort return-A states that should arm (outcomes 1/15 and 0/16 when disarmed, vs the unexpired gate's 12/4 and 14/2) AND at late B2 checkpoint-32 states that should not arm (correctly disarmed at the same profile). What DOES differ between those situations is visible in the observed stream one window further back. At a genuine return onset, the segment that disagrees with the archive is LONG: the intervening reversed segment fills both the local window (last 26 events) and the preceding window (the 26 events before it), so span-majority disagreement against the archive is stable in both windows - the archive rule has not described the stream for at least 52 events, and a newest event that is archive-concordant and reference-opposed is the first evidence of a return to a rule the learner has not seen for a full intervening segment. Late in B1 or B2, the archive rule was current recently: the preceding window still contains (B1: the tail of the original segment; B2: the tail of the return-A segment) a majority of archive-rule events, so preceding-window disagreement is NOT stable even though local disagreement is - the archive-concordant newest event there is a flip-back within a segment whose predecessor the archive still describes. Arming recovery under stable local disagreement when disagreement is long (stable in both windows), in addition to the bounded candidate's two existing legs (no stable disagreement, or corroboration >= 2), should therefore restore return-A engagement toward the unexpired gate's level without re-arming the late states the expiry correctly disarmed: at return onset the long leg's design firing probability is approx 0.85-0.90 per state (see threshold_justification), while at checkpoint-32 B1/B2 states it fires only when sparse per-span majorities in the preceding window err in the same direction on a strict majority of comparable spans (design approx 0.10-0.20). The abstention leg is NOT changed: it stays disarmed under stable disagreement exactly as in the bounded candidate, so a non-engaging return state still acts through recent8 instead of abstaining - a pre-registered tradeoff graded under criteria 3 and 4, not excused. Residual failure modes are pre-registered, not hidden: preceding-window span majorities are computed from only ~2-4 events per span and can fail to register a genuinely long disagreement on some return states (the corroboration leg remains as the fallback there); the preceding window is a subset of the archive it is compared against, biasing its majorities toward agreement and therefore against the long flag (a conservative bias, against arming); a late window whose preceding window happens to register stable disagreement can still re-arm recovery late; and a return after a SHORT intervening segment (fewer than 52 events) cannot arm through the long leg at all - this simulator's return geometry (a 64-event intervening segment) is inside the leg's scope, and the scope limit is stated, not hidden.
limitation_evidence: BOUNDED_AUTHORITY_JOINT_RECOVERY (docs/BOUNDED_AUTHORITY_JOINT_RECOVERY.md, graded Failed 2026-10-31, cohorts 342003-family / 343001-family now INSPECTED): criterion 2 (engagement) FAILs on the additional cohort - recovery TAKEN at only 2 of 6 return-A onset states (required >= 3), with 3 of 6 would-fire-but-disarmed, all at recent_concordant_count == 1, one short of the >= 2 corroboration threshold, both checkpoint-2 joint states among them (disarmed-state outcomes 1/15 and 0/16 vs the unexpired joint candidate's 12/4 and 14/2 in those states); criterion 4 (return-A harm) FAILs on the additional cohort (66 vs guard 87 PASS but vs the 60-percent-of-recent8 ceiling 52.2 FAIL - disarmed return states act through stale recent8 because abstention is disarmed at a return by the same flag); criterion 5 (PRIMARY release) FAILs development / PASSes additional. Criteria 1, 3, 6, 7 PASS on both cohorts except as stated. NOT a Regression.

Same experiment, starvation mechanism localized from the decision records: on the development cohort the identical authority condition cost nothing (return checkpoint-2 corroboration counts 4/2/2, engagement 6 of 6, pooled onset identical to the unexpired joint baseline on the same cohorts), while on the additional cohort 0 of 3 return-A states engaged at checkpoint 2. Return-A pooled successes: candidate 30 vs the unexpired joint candidate's 64 and cumulative's 74 on the same additional cells. The corroboration count is structurally weakest exactly at checkpoint 2, where only 2 of the last 8 events follow the returned rule and the other 6 are the preceding reversed segment, whose flip-back concordance realized at approx 0.08-0.17 per event in the graded records.

Same experiment, the confound that forces a NEW signal rather than a re-threshold: the recorded profile (joint_count 1, opposed_count 1, concordant_count 1, recent_concordant_count 1, stable_disagreement set) occurs both at additional return-A onset states that were disarmed (seeds 343001 and 343041 at checkpoint 2) and at late B2 checkpoint-32 states that were correctly disarmed (development seed 342003, additional seed 343001). No threshold on joint_count, opposed_count, concordant_count, or recent_concordant_count separates those states; the preceding experiment's one armed late state (development B2-32, seed 342021) sat at recent_concordant_count == 2, the return threshold itself. Any fix must read evidence the existing counts do not contain.

JOINT_CONCORDANCE_RECOVERY (docs/JOINT_CONCORDANCE_RECOVERY.md, graded Failed 2026-10-30, cohorts 332003-family / 333001-family now INSPECTED): with NO authority bound, recovery engagement was 5 of 6 return-A onset states on both cohorts - the engagement level this cycle must restore - while gate persistence without expiry failed release at checkpoint 32 on both cohorts (58 vs recent8 77; 77 vs 86). The bounded candidate proved the release is attainable with an evidence-derived bound (additional checkpoint-32 successes 63 = recent8 63, 0 of 9 non-recent8 states); this cycle tests whether both halves hold at once under a non-starving bound.
Handoff section 8 standing limitations: slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge and inconsistent adaptation to changing rules remain listed persistent weaknesses.
metrics_reported: Per seed, per stage (B1, return_A, B2, control), per checkpoint, per method: successes, harmful TEST actions, failed-by-abstention count, attempted tasks.

Candidate decision record at every checkpoint, per seed: the immediate signal record exactly as in the graded guard protocol (per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, reference event count, reference majority class or null, matched flag, opposed flag; plus opposed_count, matched_count), the archive concordance record exactly as in the graded retained-recovery protocol (per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, archive event count for that span, archive majority class or null, archive-matched flag, archive-concordant flag; plus concordant_count, archive_matched_count), the per-event JOINT flag and joint_count exactly as in the graded joint protocol, and the AUTHORITY record (per local comparable span: span, local event count, local majority class or null, archive majority class or null, comparable flag, disagreeing flag; plus comparable_span_count, disagreeing_span_count, stable_disagreement flag; per preceding-window comparable span: span, preceding event count, preceding majority class or null, archive majority class or null, preceding comparable flag, preceding disagreeing flag; plus preceding_comparable_span_count, preceding_disagreeing_span_count, preceding stable_disagreement flag, long_disagreement flag; per last-8 event: span, reported class, archive-matched flag, archive-concordant flag; plus recent_concordant_count; plus which authority leg armed recovery (none / no_stable_disagreement / corroboration / long), recovery_armed flag, abstention_armed flag, recovery_would_fire flag, abstention_would_fire flag), the branch taken (retained_archive / abstained / recent8 / all_available_below_minimum), recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, and the acting source.

Engagement and authority aggregates per cohort, from the decision records alone: recovery-fired states, abstention states, recent8 states, and - separately - recovery-would-fire-but-disarmed and abstention-would-fire-but-disarmed states, among the 6 return-A onset states, the 6 B1 onset states, the 6 B2 onset states, the graded control states, and the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states; recovery states split by arming leg (no stable disagreement / corroboration / long disagreement); plus, for continuity with the preceding experiments, the states at which the graded bounded candidate's authority (no long leg) and the graded joint candidate's unexpired rule (joint_count >= 1 for recovery, opposed_count == 2 for abstention, no authority condition) would have taken a non-recent8 branch, computed from this candidate's recorded counts and flags (the counts and flags are recorded in full, so these are records-only derivations, not re-runs).
Onset harm and successes at checkpoint 0 for every stage, per seed and method, reported explicitly as a diagnostic and never pooled into any graded onset figure and never hidden.

Persistence cost: candidate abstentions, recovery engagements, would-fire-but-disarmed counts, successes, and harm at checkpoints 8 and 16 per stage, reported alongside the checkpoint-32 release figures.
Per seed TRAIN accounting, counted once regardless of checkpoints or methods: actor actions, actual harmful actions, actual productive, actual neutral, reported harmful, report label flips.
Learner-issued information-acquisition actions (frozen at 0) and any additional observations requested (frozen at 0).
Checkpoint record SHA256 and restore-replay identity for the candidate.
No pooled-only reporting: every cohort figure must be decomposable into its three per-seed rows, and every pooled criterion figure into its per-cell rows.
permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, checkpoint value, stage position, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its concordance tests, its authority condition (local window, preceding window, and acting window alike), its recovery model, or its checkpoint record. In particular the authority condition is computed from reported events and their spans only: the learner has no access to how many events have elapsed since any switch, and no threshold in this protocol is a count of post-switch events - the local and preceding windows are fixed observed-stream windows, not segment measurements.
priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4. This experiment builds directly on the graded bounded-authority failure at return onset: the expiry restored checkpoint-32 productivity (additional 63 = recent8 63; development 42 -> 56 against the unexpired gate) but its corroboration leg (recent_concordant_count >= 2 among the last 8 events) starved at checkpoint 2 on the additional cohort, where only 2 of those 8 events follow the returned rule - recovery was TAKEN at only 2 of 6 return-A onset states, 3 of 6 would-fire states were disarmed at a count of exactly 1, and return-A harm failed its ceiling because the abstention fallback is disarmed at a return by the same flag. This cycle changes exactly one thing - the recovery branch's AUTHORITY condition gains a long-disagreement leg computed from the observed stream alone - and asks whether return engagement is restored while the checkpoint-32 release survives. This cycle's headline criterion is therefore the engagement criterion (criterion 2), graded as primary; criterion 5 (release by checkpoint 32) is the co-graded guard that the fix must not break.
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the seven graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_retained_recovery, joint_concordance_recovery, bounded_authority_joint_recovery, and the abstention guard counted once) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the acting model, the immediate opposition signal, the retained archive, the archive concordance definition, the joint recovery test, the recovery model, the abstention trigger, the local-archive disagreement definition, and the corroboration condition of the graded bounded candidate are reused EXACTLY as frozen in the bounded-authority protocol (newest window 2, reference window 24, archive events[:N-26], local window last 26, opposed_count / concordant_count / joint_count definitions unchanged, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention threshold opposed_count == 2, stable_disagreement iff C >= 1 AND D * 2 > C, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2). The single new element - the long-disagreement leg of the recovery authority, built from the SAME span-majority machinery applied to the preceding 26-event window, with its strict-majority rule carried over unchanged - is informed only by the preceding experiment's published graded aggregates and decision records (its limitation evidence), never by any score of this experiment (none exist).
required_evaluation_runs: This experiment's frozen benchmark on the development cohort and on the additional cohort, exactly as registered here.
Full unit suite: python -m unittest discover -s tests

simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures recovery-branch selectivity: false engagement, false abstention, and lost productivity when nothing changed.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).
